summary: In Greek mythology, Chromis (also Chromius; Ancient Greek Χρόμις / Χρόμιος) is a Mysian ally of Priam in the Trojan War — son of Arsinoos and brother of the augur Ennomus. Homer places the pair among the Trojan allies in the Catalogue of Ships.
etymology: Ancient Greek Χρόμις (Khrómis); Homeric and handbook tradition also use Χρόμιος (Chromius) for the same Mysian captain.

sections.heading: Mysian captain beside Ennomus
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 2.858–861) and Apollodorus (Epitome 3.35) name Chromis/Chromius with Ennomus as captains of the Mysians who came to Ilios. The catalogue marks Ennomus as an augur whom Achilles would later slay in the river; Chromis himself is fixed as an allied commander rather than a named casualty in Homer's battle books.
Wikipedia's Chromis page also lists a Lapith-war centaur, a man at Phineus' court, a son of Heracles, an Aeneid companion, and several Statius Thebans — none of which is this Mysian.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id chromis-mysian is the Catalogue Mysian alone. Chromius namesakes (Neleid, Priamid, Lycian, and others) live under separate Chromius ids; see chromius-pylian and the Trojan Chromius nodes.
